Question B-007-006-002.

Why the correct answer is right: Maximum usable frequency (MUF) changes as solar radiation changes the amount and height of ionization along a path. Stronger useful ionization can support higher frequencies. Weaker ionization lowers the limit.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "The temperature of the ionosphere": Temperature alone does not set the electron density needed to refract a high-frequency (HF) wave back to Earth. Solar-driven ionization does.
- sourceIndex 2: "The speed of the winds in the upper atmosphere": Upper-atmosphere winds may move irregularities, but the MUF is governed mainly by electron density from solar radiation.
- sourceIndex 3: "The type of weather just below the ionosphere": Ordinary weather below the ionosphere affects tropospheric paths more than HF sky-wave MUF.
